newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU ministers meet to prepare jobs summit.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers meet to prepare jobs summit.

text.p: European Union social affairs ministers met on Saturday in the small Luxembourg town of Echternach to prepare for a November jobs summit which will address the plight of Europe's 18 million unemployed.

"While we should not raise expectations that the summit will by itself provide solutions for the unemployment problem in Europe, it must be able to confirm a genuine commitment of member states in favour of employment," EU Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn told ministers on Saturday.
The notes of his speech were made available to reporters.

Ministers arrived on Friday evening for the informal meeting, the first since Luxembourg took over the EU presidency on July 1, and were due to leave midday on Sunday. A news conference was scheduled for later on Saturday.

A Luxembourg official said that during a round table discussion everyone agreed "something had to be done" to boost employment, though a large majority had also warned against deregulation and "flexibility without boundries".
Employment was pushed to the top of the agenda at last month's EU summit in Amsterdam, when France agreed to an EU budget stability pact only in return for a resolution on jobs and growth.

The resolution reflected growing concern among Europe's citizens that in the austerity drive needed to get member states in shape for a single European currency, the EU was losing sight of social issues.
But diplomats said this week they expected ministers to make little progress on the idea which has been in deadlock for more than twenty years.
